title: Cohort-affinity TTL pinning with tier-aware fallback and canary cohort splits
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: We need deterministic model version pinning for cohorts (sessions/customers) that preserves canary/A-B splits while allowing graceful degradation when capacity or quality issues appear. Current pinning is session-sticky without TTL and doesn't account for tier-based fallbacks or cache warm-up, which causes large cold-cache penalties and hard-to-reproduce canary noise.

Goals: 
- Provide cohort-level pinning with TTL and decay so experiments (canary/A-B) produce stable metrics but don't permanently lock traffic.
- Support per-customer hard-pins (enterprise commitments) vs soft cohort pins (experiments).
- Make fallback hierarchical and tier-aware (region -> tier -> variant) with predictable economics and latency SLOs.
- Minimize KV cache churn and warm-up penalties during rollouts.
- Enable automated adaptive-split adjustments (skew correction) when canary quality/latency deviates.

Design summary (chosen approach): 
1) Cohort assignment and pin metadata: 
   - Cohort key: deterministic hash over (customer_id || cookie_id || session_id) with configurable namespace per-route.
   - Pin record stored in routing-store (sharded KV): {cohort_key, pinned_model_version, pin_type, pin_ts, ttl_seconds, cohort_version, cohort_hash_seed} (we store as flat fields).
   - Pin types: HARD (enterprise-level, no automatic expire), SOFT (experiment pin, TTL with decay), TRANSIENT (per-request affinity, no storage).
   - TTL semantics: SOFT pins include an initial TTL and an exponential decay function on re-pinning (repeated exposures extend TTL but with diminishing returns) to bound lifetime while preserving steady traffic during a rollout.

2) Canary cohort splits: 
   - Rollouts configured as cohort-weighted buckets rather than pure percentage-by-request. We derive bucket weights using consistent hashing with weighted ranges so the same cohort maps to the same bucket across restarts.
   - We implement cohort cohorts for canaries: small set of high-fidelity cohorts (e.g., internal orgs, beta customers) plus a probabilistic patient cohort for general population.

3) Tier-aware fallback policy (ordered): 
   - Prefer: same-region, same-tier, pinned-version (if available).
   - Fallback 1: same-region, lower-tier compatible variant (quantized/cheaper) if pinned unavailable or instance saturated.
   - Fallback 2: cross-region, same-tier compatible variant within latency budget.
   - Fallback 3: best-effort hosted variant with quality-preserving transforms (e.g., constrained max_tokens or higher temperature fallback).
   - For HARD pins we skip automated downgrade to lower-quality variants unless manual override or emergency degrade mode is enabled.

4) Soft-pin override under pressure: 
   - Soft pins are advisory; routing can temporarily route away if local capacity saturated or p99 latency > configured threshold. The system records override events (override_count, override_reason) so the pin TTL can be shortened (decay) after an override to allow subsequent cohorts to rebalance.

5) Cache warm-up and KV cache considerations: 
   - To avoid cold prefix penalties, the router will do two-stage steering for newly pinned cohorts: a small fraction of their traffic is routed to the pinned model prior to full split (cache warm-up window). Warm-up size is configurable per rollout.
   - Eviction policy for routing-store: use LRU with pin-type prioritization (HARD > SOFT > TRANSIENT). We will batch writes to the routing-store to reduce write pressure during large percent rollouts.

6) Metrics and telemetry: 
   - Per-cohort and per-model-version metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, generation quality score (where available), token-cost per request, cache-miss rate.
   - Canary evaluation window: min requests and min unique cohorts per bucket to consider metric stable.
   - Alerts: automatic regression detection when canary cohort quality drops by configured delta or latency increases above SLO.

7) Adaptive split control: 
   - If canary shows regression (quality or latency), automated policies reduce cohort weights by multiplying canary weight by corrective factor and extend warm-up on rebalancing. The system attempts two automatic reductions before pausing rollout and paging on-call.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Stateless vs stateful pinning: Stateless percentage-by-request is simpler but produces noisy cohort coverage for canaries. We chose cohort-stateful pins for reproducibility at the cost of KV-state complexity.
- Hard vs soft pins: Hard pins protect enterprise contracts but reduce our ability to adapt under pressure. We allow explicit admin overrides and emergency degrade modes.
- Cache warm-up increases short-term cost to prevent long-term quality noise; we added a configurable warm-up budget.

Implementation plan (milestones): 
- M1 (2 weeks): Routing-store schema + KV sharding + API to read/write pin records (migration plan for existing pins).
- M2 (2 weeks): Cohort hashing library + consistent-weighted buckets + rollout config schema changes.
- M3 (3 weeks): Fallback engine and soft-pin override logic + override auditing events.
- M4 (2 weeks): Warm-up steering, batched writes, LRU prioritization.
- M5 (2 weeks): Metrics instrumentation + canary evaluation automation + alerting rules.
- M6 (1 week): E2E tests, chaos test (simulate region outage), and staged rollout to internal orgs.

Rollout and migration: 
- Start by enabling SOFT pins for internal and beta cohorts only. 
- Run shadow mode (routing decisions computed but not enforced) for 1 week to validate metrics and override counts. 
- After validation, enable active routing for non-HARD cohorts on a single region, with 5% cohort coverage and warm-up staging.

Rollout safety and rollback criteria: 
- Immediate rollback if: canary p99 latency increases by >40% and absolute p99 > 2x configured SLO, or error rate >1% absolute increase, or quality score drift >5% with >1000 eval requests.
- Auto-shrink if minor regressions: reduce canary weight by 50% and extend warm-up by 2x.

Operational notes: 
- Console exposure: add cohort mapping view and per-cohort pin audit trail, plus admin override controls.
- Data retention: pin audit logs retained for 90 days.
- Cost: warm-up increases token use — include cost accounting per rollout in the Console.

Open questions: 
- How to surface model-variant semantic compatibility (we currently rely on curated compatibility matrix maintained by model onboarding).
- TTL decay parameters: default safe values proposed but needs product sign-off.
- Backfill strategy for existing permanent pins: convert to HARD or SOFT with migration TTL.

acceptance_criteria: Routing-store correctly returns same pinned version for a cohort across restarts
Fallback ordering respects tier boundaries and records override events
Shadow mode telemetry matches simulated active routing within 1% variance
Canary evaluation automation triggers alerts on regressions and auto-shrink behavior functions as documented
Console shows cohort-to-version mapping and override audit trail
